subject: Input: xpad - add opt-in 8BitDo initialization bypass
author: Kasper Olesen

upstream.vanilla_file_line: drivers/input/joystick/xpad.c:1809-1844 in the 6.18.49 release commit 1c732c6b94f0 (linux-6.18.y); drivers/input/joystick/xpad.c:1790-1810 in v7.2.3 (58e7295cfecad) -- same shape in both, and neither has a skip_8bitdo_init or any 2dc8-specific bypass. This is a fork-only addition; no vanilla equivalence claim applies.

provenance_doc_ref: none -- this commit postdates docs/patch-provenance.md's baseline by five years; not previously dispositioned.

impact.effect_if_absent: With the module parameter left at its default (false, which is what happens if we do NOT carry this commit), there is zero behaviour change: xpad_start_input()'s XTYPE_XBOX360 branch condition `xpad->xtype == XTYPE_XBOX360 && !(skip_8bitdo_init && ...)` reduces to exactly the unconditional `xpad->xtype == XTYPE_XBOX360` that both v6.18.49 and v7.2.3 already have, for every device including 2dc8:3106. If we DO carry it (this record's recommendation), the only observable effect is a new sysfs knob `/sys/module/xpad/parameters/skip_8bitdo_init` (and an insmod/modprobe option of the same name) that a user or a MiSTer community script can set to 1 to omit the Xbox-360 vendor init control request for USB ID 2dc8:3106 only, as an A/B tool for the reconnect-failure regression tracked in fork issue #84 (not readable from this session -- GitHub issues are blocked per env.md/worker-preamble). Not carrying it means MiSTer users have no way to test that A/B switch locally; carrying it costs nothing to users who never touch the parameter.
affected_hardware: 8BitDo Ultimate Wireless / Pro 2 Wired Controller and any other USB device presenting as 2dc8:3106 -- the fork commit's own message flags that some 8BitDo Ultimate RECEIVER dongles (not just the wired/paired controller this xpad_device[] row names) share this exact VID:PID, so the switch's scope is USB-ID-based, not device-model-based

userspace_coupling.main_mister_ref: grep of $S/main (Main_MiSTer, HEAD 6cda9cc546c4, depth 120) for '2dc8', '8BitDo'/'8bitdo', '0x3106', 'skip_8bitdo' finds only input.cpp:5852 and input.cpp:6130-6131 ('// Menu button on 8BitDo Receiver in D-Input mode' / 'if (ev.code == 9 && input[dev].vid == 0x2dc8 && (input[dev].pid == 0x3100 || input[dev].pid == 0x3104))'). Those PIDs are 0x3100/0x3104 (evdev D-Input-mode variants), not 0x3106 (the XTYPE_XBOX360 row this commit targets), and Main_MiSTer references neither the module parameter name nor PID 0x3106 anywhere. No coupling to this commit's behavior.

forward_port.effort: trivial to fold as a fifth delta into 0017-xpad-mister-deltas.patch. Verified by dry-run and real apply in a temp tree: `patch -p1 -F0` of 0017 onto the 6.18.49 release-commit xpad.c applies all 18 hunks with only line-number offsets (0-2 lines, no fuzz); the fork's own two-hunk diff then applies cleanly on top of that 0017-patched file at -F0 -- hunk 1 (the skip_8bitdo_init module_param block) applies at line 129 with ZERO offset because 0017 already declares `cpoll`'s module_param immediately above the fork's insertion point and 0017 makes no edits between that point and the top of the file; hunk 2 (the xpad_start_input() XTYPE_XBOX360 guard) applies at line 2122 with a 23-line offset (0017 adds code earlier in the file, e.g. MAP_VADER5/MAP_VADER4 bit defines and the Flydigi V2 block) but ZERO fuzz -- the surrounding context (the two-line usb_control_msg_recv comment, the dummy[20] buffer, the bRequest/bmRequestType/wValue/wIndex layout) is byte-identical, because 0017 never touches xpad_start_input()'s body. Same result against v7.2.3 with the linux-patches-beta copy of 0017 (0017 hunks apply with larger negative offsets, ~-31 to -34 lines, reflecting the shorter 7.x file; the fork hunks then apply at -F0 with offsets -34/-10 and zero fuzz), and against de25nano's linux-patches (a symlink to the same 0017 file, so identical result). All three series confirmed at -F0 with zero fuzz -- see notes for the exact hunk lines quoted.

notes:
CARRIED. AUTHORED 2026-09-11 (Wave 3) as 0017's delta 5 -- carried_mode 're-implemented' because 0017 is a curated multi-delta patch regenerated pristine->patched against 6.18.49, not a textual carry of the fork's two-hunk diff. The paragraphs below were written in Wave 1, when the fold was still planned; they describe what was to be done and are kept because that is exactly what WAS done -- 0017's header 'Delta 5 fold' block records the measured apply. The new delta was inserted immediately after the existing `cpoll` module_param block (0017's own insertion point for that block, board/mister/de10nano/linux-patches/0017-xpad-mister-deltas.patch's second hunk) and a second hunk added at xpad_start_input()'s XTYPE_XBOX360 guard, per the fork's own two-hunk diff quoted above. The default value stays `false` so 0017's export/lint round-trip and every existing behaviour are unaffected -- confirmed structurally: the condition `xpad->xtype == XTYPE_XBOX360 && !(skip_8bitdo_init && idVendor==0x2dc8 && idProduct==0x3106)` is logically equivalent to the unconditional XTYPE_XBOX360 branch whenever skip_8bitdo_init is false, for every device including 2dc8:3106.

THE ISSUE-#84 REGRESSION ITSELF IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS RECORD, NEEDS-VERIFICATION. This item is not about whether the reconnect failure exists or whether skipping the vendor-init request fixes it -- that is a hardware-gated question this session cannot answer (no affected-controller hardware here, and the fork commit's own message says 'No affected-controller hardware validation yet' upstream either). Fork issue #84 is unreadable from this session (GitHub issues/PR discussions blocked per worker-preamble.md 'Network' section and env.md); the commit message's own summary ('the reconnect failure reported in MiSTer issue 84... Its role in the reported regression is unconfirmed') is the only description available. Do NOT read this record's 'carried' disposition as confirming or denying the #84 bug -- it only confirms the module-parameter mechanism is safe to carry with a default-off value. A human should paste issue #84's body/comments if a verdict on the actual regression (not just the A/B tooling) is needed.

THE COMMIT'S OWN CAVEAT ON DEVICE-ID SCOPE. The commit message states: 'Some Ultimate receivers share this ID, so this is an experimental A/B switch, not a permanent quirk.' i.e. 2dc8:3106 is not uniquely the wired/paired '8BitDo Ultimate Wireless / Pro 2 Wired Controller' xpad_device[] row names -- some 8BitDo Ultimate wireless RECEIVER dongles also enumerate as 2dc8:3106, and skip_8bitdo_init (if a user opts in) would affect those too, for better or worse. This is exactly why the change is a runtime-toggleable module param and not an unconditional quirk-table change, and why the record's severity is 'none' (default-off) rather than 'feature-loss' or similar -- there is no behaviour to lose by default.
